archetype.name: Pretender (pass-defense first)
archetype.definition: A 3-2 team that has been outscored by 19 points, propped up by three one-score wins and a pass defense that is better than everything around it.

report.headline: Three close wins mask a team outscored by 19 that can't run or block
report.take:
Cleveland under first-year coach Todd Monken looks like the last two Browns teams with a slightly better offense. The 2025 team had the league's third-best defense by EPA and the 31st-ranked offense. This version has a solid pass defense (4th in pass EPA allowed, 5th in sack rate) attached to an offense that ranks 25th in EPA and 27th in scoring. The difference is the record. At 3-2 they sit level with Cincinnati and Pittsburgh, a game behind Baltimore, yet their point differential is -3.8 a game, 25th in the league, and their net EPA is 23rd.

The record comes from the margins. All three wins came by four points or fewer: 23-19 at Tampa, 21-18 over Carolina, 27-24 over Pittsburgh. The two losses came by 24 and 5. Their 1.26 wins over expected ranks 5th, and that kind of surplus rarely survives a full season. Turnovers haven't driven it either way: the differential is -0.2 a game and they have six takeaways. What actually swung those wins was Deshaun Watson's passing on good days. He posted +10.4 pass EPA at Tampa and +9.2 against Pittsburgh. Against Jacksonville (-5.6) and the Jets (-12.5) the passing game collapsed.

The numbers hide how fragile that passing game is. Cleveland passes 4.7 points more often than expected, 4th-most, partly because the run game is broken: 3.12 yards a carry, a 30.8% run success rate (last), and 1.59 yards before contact (31st). The line actually allows pressure at a low rate (7th), yet Watson has been sacked on 10.3% of dropbacks, worst in the league. Eight of the 19 sacks came in one game against the Jets. A modest pressure rate paired with a league-worst sack rate points at the quarterback holding the ball and the protection failing to finish, more than at a line constantly beaten. Add a league-worst 9.8 penalties a game, five of them on the line, and drives die on their own.

On defense, the pass numbers are real but sit on a weak foundation against the run. Opponents lose EPA when they throw, yet the run defense is 29th in EPA allowed and last in explosive run rate, with a 29th-ranked missed-tackle rate. That will now be tested without interior linemen Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., both out, and Kalia Davis on IR. The schedule offers relief, with Tennessee, New Orleans, Houston and Indianapolis still ahead. Still, this is a roughly .450 team whose record is a game ahead of its play.

strengths.title: Pass defense that finishes pressure
strengths.body: Cleveland ranks 4th in pass EPA allowed and 5th in sack rate even though its pressure rate is only 27th. When it gets home, it gets the quarterback down, with 16 sacks in five games. The pass-defense profile fits the franchise's recent history (3rd in defensive EPA in 2025, 1st in 2023), so it is more than a five-game blip. The low pressure rate does mean the sack total leans on conversion, which can cool off.

strengths.title: Red-zone stands keep games close
strengths.body: Opponents score touchdowns on only 42.9% of red-zone trips, 4th-best. Despite a 20th-ranked yardage defense, that keeps the defense 14th in points allowed. It is also a big part of why so many games have stayed within one score. Red-zone rates are noisy over five games, so treat it as helpful rather than bankable.

strengths.title: Playable passing when upright
strengths.body: Even with the sacks, the pass offense ranks 18th in EPA, far ahead of the 31st-ranked run game. On clean days it carried them, with +10.4 at Tampa and +9.2 against Pittsburgh. Targets are spread across Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion and tight end Harold Fannin Jr., at 29, 29 and 27, so there is no single point of failure.

concerns.title: Record built on one-score luck
concerns.body: Cleveland is 3-2 with a -19 point differential, and its three wins came by a combined 10 points. A 1.26 wins-over-expected mark (5th) says the record is about a game ahead of the play. That regresses unless the efficiency improves, and the underlying EPA (23rd net) gives little sign it will.

concerns.title: No run game, too many sacks
concerns.body: The ground game is last in success rate and 31st in EPA and yards before contact, so the offense has no way to stay on schedule. Meanwhile Watson takes sacks at the league's worst rate despite a 7th-ranked pressure rate, which points at sack-proneness more than a porous line. Tytus Howard is questionable and Teven Jenkins is out, so the protection could get worse before it gets better.

concerns.title: Soft run defense, now thinner inside
concerns.body: The run defense is 29th in EPA allowed, worst in explosive run rate, and 29th in missed-tackle rate. That was before losing Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., with Kalia Davis already on IR and linebacker Carson Schwesinger, a 100%-snap player, questionable with an ankle sprain. Against run-first opponents this is the defense's real vulnerability.

trend.note: Pass EPA by game reads -5.6, +10.4, +2.1, +9.2, -12.5, and the record rose and fell with it. The latest game, an eight-sack, two-turnover loss to the Jets, was the worst offensive showing of the year.

nextGame.headline: Lamar-less Ravens can still run straight at a gutted interior
nextGame.body:
Baltimore runs more than expected (-6 pass rate over expected, 27th) and does it well: 4.8 yards a carry (4th) and a 6th-ranked run EPA. That aims straight at Cleveland's weakest unit. The Ravens' pass defense is middling, 28th in pressure rate and 21st in sack rate, which is the softest rush Watson will have seen. Their secondary also leaks deep (25th in deep EPA) and to opposing WR1s (31st in EPA allowed). Underneath they are stingy, 3rd in short-pass EPA, so the Browns need to hit shots rather than dink.

Availability shapes this game on both sides. Lamar Jackson is listed out with an ankle sprain, though described as doing better, and Tyler Huntley started Week 5. Center Cam Jurgens and edge Trey Hendrickson are also out. Cleveland is missing DTs Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., and Schwesinger, Howard, Concepcion and Judkins are all questionable. If Concepcion is out, more of the deep work falls to Boston and Fannin. The forecast is early, with 12 mph wind and 18 mph gusts, which is not enough to change the game on its own.

keyMatchups.title: Ravens run game vs. thin DL
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore is 6th in run EPA and success rate, and Cleveland is 29th against the run and last in explosive runs allowed, now without two rotation DTs. With a backup quarterback, Baltimore has every reason to lean on this edge and control the clock.

keyMatchups.title: Watson's sacks vs. a soft rush
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland's league-worst sack rate meets a Ravens defense that is 28th in pressure and 21st in sack rate, and Hendrickson is out. If Watson still takes three or more sacks here, the problem is plainly his.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots to the WR1
keyMatchups.body: Baltimore allows 0.871 EPA on deep throws (25th) and 0.76 a play to opposing WR1s (31st), but only -0.144 on short throws (3rd). Denzel Boston, tied for the team lead in targets, is the obvious beneficiary, especially if Concepcion misses time.

nextGame.watch: Whether Baltimore just runs it 35 times at the depleted Browns interior, and whether Watson can take a deep shot without taking a sack.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the record to drift back toward the play. The one-score surplus should fade, and a 25th-ranked offense without a run game will lose more coin flips than it wins. The schedule is the counterweight. Tennessee (0-5), New Orleans and Houston (1-4) and Indianapolis (2-3) are all still ahead, while five division games, including two each against Baltimore and Cincinnati, carry the risk. The pass defense is the sustainable piece. The sack-taking is partly fixable if Watson gets the ball out, but the run game shows no sign of life, and the run defense is likely to get worse while the DTs are out.

Realistically this is a 5-7 or 6-6 team the rest of the way, landing near .500 overall. That is enough to hang around a muddled AFC North but not enough to be taken seriously as a contender.
swingFactors: Watson's sack rate and big-game variance
Return of Graham and Hall to the interior DL

bets.reason: Baltimore is likely on its backup QB, runs more than expected and owns the clock (32 minutes a game), facing a Browns offense that scores 18.6 a game. Cleveland's 4th-ranked red-zone defense and Baltimore's 3rd-ranked short-pass defense both push drives toward field goals.

Without Jackson, Jurgens and Hendrickson, Baltimore's 5th-ranked net EPA overstates what takes the field. Cleveland is 3-2 ATS as an underdog every week and gets this division game at home with a pass defense ranked 4th. The run-defense injuries keep this a modest edge, not a strong one.

confidence.note: Five games, a first-year coach, and heavy injury uncertainty on both sides, including Jackson's status.
